items.title: Uber’s Driverless Lucid Tests Begin. Lucid’s Robotaxi Order Now Tops Two Years of Deliveries
items.summary: Key TakeawaysUber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity robotaxis in the Bay Area, ahead of a commercial launch now planned for the first quarter of 2027. Uber also has robotaxi deals with Rivian and others, but its order for at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles is bigger than everything Lucid delivered in 2025 and the first nine months of 2026 combined.

items.title: Lucid Sinks 13% in a Week as the Tech Selloff Hits EV Stocks. Seaport Sets a $1 Target
items.summary: Key TakeawaysLucid fell 13% in the past week, mostly in Friday’s tech selloff, which also hit Rivian and Tesla. Seaport initiated coverage with a Sell and a $1 target the same morning Lucid, Nuro and Uber began driverless robotaxi tests.

items.title: Anthropic Broke Its $83 IPO Price. What Did Facebook Do Next?
items.summary: Anthropic (ANT) closed at $82.79 on Wednesday, Nov 25. That is 0.3% below its $83 IPO price. It is also 14.8% below its $97.17 first close, only five trading days in. So what happened to other big listings that broke this fast.

items.title: Bill Gurley: Investors Weren’t “Scrambling to Actually Own Anthropic.” That’s a Problem for Amazon and Alphabet
items.summary: Key TakeawaysAnthropic fell below its $83 IPO price on Tuesday, its fourth day of trading. Bill Gurley says few of the IPO’s buyers planned to hold the stock.

items.title: Lucid Group (LCID) Starts Driverless Robotaxi Testing, Is It A Bargain?
items.summary: Lucid Group (LCID) just moved its Gravity robotaxi program into fully driverless testing with Nuro and Uber in the San Francisco Bay Area, marking a concrete step toward commercial autonomous ride hailing. Lucid Group’s latest robotaxi milestone comes after a rough stretch for investors, with the 1-year total shareholder return down about 80% and the 5-year total shareholder return down close to 99%. items.title: Nvidia is cheap on paper, so why won't the market buy it?
items.summary: Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia giving back about half of its Jensen Huang rally and why a stock growing sales 60% to 70% can trade at 10 times earnings, whether the Alice Wong affair was a "hit job," and what next week's Senate testimony means for the stock.
